      void Module.addHandler(Class<? extends IMessageHandler> handler)
      Adds the given handler class to this module.
      void Module.addHandlers(Collection<Class<? extends IMessageHandler>> handlers)
      Calls Module.addHandler(Class) for each handler class (see the javadoc for that method for more details).
      Set<Class<?>> Module.apply(MessageSink... sinks)
      The same as Module.apply(MessageSink[], String[], Map) except that no keywords will be specified, meaning that it will attempt to apply every handler to the group of given sinks.
      Set<Class<?>> Module.apply(MessageSink[] sinks, String[] keywords)
      The same as Module.apply(MessageSink[], String[], Map) except that no additional information will be given to the handlers when they are created.
      Set<Class<?>> Module.apply(MessageSink[] sinks, String[] keywords, Map<String,Object> properties)
      Create a new instance of each of the handler classes contained in the module and adds them to the appropriate MessageSinks from the set given to this method as a parameter.

      X      		 MessageContext.getRequest(Class<X> type, IMessageHandler handler)
